 11/17 Preview – Gustafsson Expected To Return + Power Play Entries, Setup, Overtime History
 By Zach Dooley 
 6 hours ago 
 212 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (5-11-2) @ Boston Bruins (8-10-1)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 19/84
 WHEN: Tuesday, November 17 @ 4:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: TD Garden – Boston, MA
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: The Kings begin a five-game roadtrip tonight, starting with four straight on the East Coast, as they visit the Boston Bruins at TD Garden. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Forward Alex Laferriere scored the only Kings goal in a 4-1 loss to the Bruins earlier this season, with defenseman Brandt Clarke and forward Adrian Kempe collecting assists. Clarke has five points (1-4-5) in six career games played against Boston, including an overtime game-winning goal here in 2024, while Kempe leads the team with four points (0-4-4) over the last five matchups. 
 KINGS VITALS: The Kings held a full-team morning skate today at TD Garden, following yesterday’s practice day at Harvard. 
 Goaltender Darcy Kuemper was off the ice first this morning and it looks like he will start the trip opener for the Kings in Boston. Kuemper stopped 45 of the 49 shots he faced against the Bruins last season, coming in a pair of 2-1 overtime losses. The veteran netminder has a lifetime record of 3-7-3 against the Bruins, with a .900 save percentage and a 2.65 goals-against average. 
 Here is a projected lineup for tonight’s game, based on today’s morning skate and yesterday’s practice day –
 Turcotte – Laferriere – Kempe
Fiala – Byfield – Zuccarello
Moore – Haula – Armia
Lee – Laughton – Perry
 Gustafsson – Clarke
Edmundson – Doughty
Anderson – Dumoulin
 Kuemper
Forsberg
 Look for defenseman Erik Gustafsson to re-enter the Kings lineup tonight, after he missed the last three due to an injury. Defenseman Cody Ceci is expected to check out of the lineup, joining forward Samuel Helenius as the players on the ice late after today’s morning skate. Forward Artemi Panarin remains away from the team due to the passing of his grandfather and also will not play tonight. 
 BRUINS VITALS: Boston concludes a four-game homestand this evening against the Kings, entering with a 1-2-0 record, following a win over Florida and defeats to Montreal and Minnesota. 
 Per Bella Fraser of BostonBruins.com, here’s how tonight’s opponent lined up last time out versus the Wild – 
 Bruins warmup lines: Peterka-Zacha-Pastrnak Eyssimont-Minten-Geekie Mittlestadt-E. Lindholm-Khusnutdinov Jeannot-Poitras-Kastelic H. Lindholm-McAvoy Zadorov-Borgen Brunet-Clifton Swayman DiPietro
 — Belle Fraser (@bellefraser1) November 14, 2026 
 Forward David Pastrnak led his team with two points (1-1-2) in his team’s victory at Crypto.com Arena and has 12 points (5-7-12) in nine games against the Kings over the last five seasons. Former Kings forward Tanner Jeannot has skated in all 20 games this season, totaling five points (1-4-5), while former Kings prospect Mikey Eyssimont was recently recalled from the AHL and scored his first goal of the season in his season debut on November 8.
 Storyline Of The Day – The Gus Bus 
Welcome back, Erik Gustafsson!
 Gustafsson has been out for the last three games due to an undisclosed injury, but he’s practiced with the team now three times, between true practices and morning skates, and Peter Laviolette confirmed this morning that he will return to the lineup this evening. Gustafsson said he feels good and is “glad to be back” as the Kings begin the trip. 
 There have been several areas lacking of late for the Kings, but one of the biggest has been connectivity between the defensemen and the forwards on the breakout and in transition. It’s felt like last season in that regard. Gustafsson brings that in his game.
 “I think that’s what Gus’ strengths are, he’s a good puck mover, he’s a good skater, he goes back and gets pucks,” Laviolette said of Gustafsson. “He helps us get out of our zone and through the neutral zone a little bit cleaner.”
 Against Calgary, the goals against came directly off of turnovers by Kings defensemen, though that’s not necessarily the area Laviolette talking about. Those were both extremely preventable plays, regardless of personnel, that needed to be executed better. With Gustafsson, it’s the more routine sequences where you notice him. Gustafsson ranks second on the Kings behind only Brandt Clarke when you look at the metrics on controlled zone exits and controlled zone entries. The transportation element from the backend has lacked without Gustafsson and it’s shown up when he’s been in the lineup.
 The other area he has helped the team has been on the power play. With Artemi Panarin out of the lineup again tonight, I expect that we will see Gustafsson placed back on the top unit. In the six games that Gustafsson has skated on PP1, the Kings have clicked at 32.0 percent, the sixth-best number in the NHL. They were at 14.8 percent before and at 12.5 percent since. Again, it isn’t just one player, but Gustafsson does bring a left shot to the point on that unit and he’s a willing shooter, which is something that can open up additional lanes. Maybe the handedness factors in more than you’d think, too, as the unit seemed to operate more dangerously with Kempe up top as well. 
 Look for Gustafsson to run up top, with Kevin Fiala operating in a spot we’ve often seen him, on the left flank, with Adrian Kempe’s shot playing on the right side. 
 All in all, there are multiple areas in which Gustafsson helps the team, most of which come with regards to when the Kings have the puck, looking to create offensively.
 “It’s a little bit of everything, I think he’s a positive influence when he’s on the ice with regards to offense,” Laviolette added. “It can come in different ways. He’s good on the power play. I think he’s good on the rush, getting out of our end, good on the rush adding to it and he brings something in the offensive zone as well. There’s a lot of things that increase if he’s available.”
 Gustafsson is a welcomed addition. Credit to Laviolette for pushing in that direction over the summer, considering his familiarity with him, with an understanding of his fit within the way he wants his teams to play. He’s been good and it’s nice to see him back in the lineup tonight. 
 3 To Watch For – 
– As noted above, among the many areas in need of an uptick, the power play sans Panarin certainly was not the same.
 The biggest struggle seemed to be on the zone entries and establishing controlled possession in the offensive end off of the zone entries, when faced with pressure. One of Panarin’s many gifts is his composure when pressured and his ability to find soft areas on the ice to control possession. Even if it takes a couple of seconds, Panarin is never rattled when pressured and his ability to settle things down allows the unit to get set up offensively. I thought the Kings really missed that element specifically against the Flames, which they agreed with. 
 “Without Bread, it’s tough, everybody knows when he’s on the ice and he creates a lot of space for his linemates, just being out there, so I think for us, it’s about trying to be simpler and getting it behind that first layer of defense,” forward Alex Laferriere said. “It starts with me. I had two or three turnovers on entries last game, so I think just trying to get it in behind that first line and we’ve got guys like Q and Kev who are really good in puck battles. As long as we can get it down there, we’re going to win pucks back.”
 In terms of personnel, as noted above, Kevin Fiala will be on that unit, along with Gustafsson, Laferriere, Kempe and Quinton Byfield. I think that the entries really should be more of an area of strength, considering how well most of those players skate with the puck. Looking at the in-zone setup, it’s tricky, because things often operated directly through Panarin on the left side.
 He’s such a crafty playmaker who operates on instincts that it’s hard to replace him. Having said that, Fiala is a creative player in his own right. Just because Panarin is out, doesn’t mean the players are looking to overhaul anything.
 “Getting Kevin on the left side, he’s a hell of a player too and it’s a little bit different, he can attack more, because he’s a lefty,” Gustafsson said. “I don’t think it changes my view from the top, but I get to drag it a little bit more and pass it over to him and he can attack more going downhill. Then, he also has Q in the middle and Kempe on the right side for a one-timer. It looked good in the morning and we’ve got to bring it tonight.”
 Boston enters tonight’s game just outside of the Top-10 in penalty-killing percentage this season at 80.3 percent, but Los Angeles had two opportunities, between one true power play and a 5-on-4 with the goaltender pulled on matching penalties – in the third period when these teams met in October and didn’t get it done on those chances. Said it a million times but special teams are often the difference when you have a team that doesn’t score consistently 5-on-5. It remains an opportunity. 
 – If history is any indicator, we can probably expect to see overtime tonight in Boston. 
 Each of the last eight games between these two teams at TD Garden have gone beyond the scheduled 60 minutes. The Kings have won five of those eight games, though the Bruins have won each of the last two. As noted, defenseman Brandt Clarke scored the overtime game-winning goal in 2024, while forward Trevor Moore had the shootout, game-deciding goal during the 2022-23 season. 
 The last time a Kings/Bruins game at TD Garden ended after three periods came on December 18, 2016, a 1-0 Boston regulation victory. Alec Martinez, who will be in the booth tonight, was in the lineup that night, logging 21:02 on the blueline. A crazy streak and we’ll see if it continues again into tonight’s matchup.
 – Lastly, speaking of Martinez, one final plug for the broadcast tonight, as he joins John Kelly in the booth in Boston. 
 Shared this last night, but adding in this interview below one more time with the man himself. 
 Think it should be a pretty cool fit and I’m excited to see how he translates into the lead analyst role tonight.
 Kings and Bruins as a four-game trip gets underway at TD Garden. Has almost always been a competitive game between these two teams, especially here in Massachusetts. See if that continues, despite the current state of things for Los Angeles.
